 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Yashraj Bardhan, Advocate
For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Damodar Prasad Tiwary, APP  ========================================

 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HARISH KUMAR  ORAL ORDER 2 10-01-2024 Heard Mr. Yashraj Bardhan, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and Mr. Damodar Prasad Tiwary, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1574 of 2022 giving rise to Trial No. 3347 of 2023, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. It is alleged that the marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with the opposite party no. 2 on 18.02.2018 as per the Hindu rites and rituals.

At the time of marriage sufficient dowry was given to the petitioner, however, the accused persons Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.81595 of 2023(2)
dt.10-01-2024 kept on demanding dowry.
On account of non-fulfillment of the same, she was tortured in various ways and lastly ousted from the matrimonial house on 11.10.2021, leading to the filing of present complaint case.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been serving Indian Navy and, in fact, the complainant is in the habit of creating nuisance and it is she,
who does not want to live with her in- laws, resulting into institution of a Divorce Case no. 253 of 2021, pending before the learned Principle Judge, Saran at Chapra.

He further submits that the present complaint case is nothing but an outburst of aforenoted Divorce Case no. 253 of 2021, which has been instituted much prior to the institution of the present complaint.

He next submits that now the opposite party is also getting Rs. 12,000/- per month from the petitioner on account of a complaint made by the opposite party no. 2 in the naval office of the petitioner.
He lastly submits that the relationship between the parties has become so worsen that there is no chance of reconciliation.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposed the pre-arrest bail application and submits that the petitioner being husband is responsible for all sort of tortures Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.81595 of 2023(2) dt.10-01-2024 and demand of dowry.

6. Regard being had to the submissions made on behalf of the parties and considering the fact that the petitioner's case for grant of divorce is pending prior to the institution the present complaint,
that apart, the opposite party no. 2 is getting Rs. 12,000/- for her maintenance, let the petitioner above named be released on bail, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order, upon furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate in connection with Complaint Case no.
1574 of 2022, subject to the conditions laid down in Section 438(2) Cr.P.C. with the further condition that one of the bailors shall be the own/close family members of the petitioner.

(Harish Kumar, J) supratim/-
